claims.claim: The independent final evaluation completed, was qualified, and reports successful specified checks; qualification is not a superiority or shifted-validity result.
The final study comprises eight seeds, six conditions (logistic-normal IID, Dirichlet IID, shifted Dirichlet at K=3 and 8), and alpha=0.05,0.10,0.20. All recorded cases are complete.
Final seeds are 1009,1013,1019,1021,1031,1033,1039,1049; train/calibration/test sizes are 1024/512/2048 with six covariates.
Positive observed continuous compositions, not categorical labels or latent probabilities, are the response. The fixed Helmert ILR basis has K-1 coordinates.
The design uses intercept, raw features, squares, sines and x0*x1. Center and log-residual ridge penalties are 1 and 10; intercept penalty is 1e-8; residual floor is .02.
Centers are clipped to [-100,100] and positive base and corrected scales to [1e-4,100]. The base log-residual fit uses in-sample residuals; correction moments are cross-fitted.
Three-fold training permutations use random seed 0. Moment features use standard deviation floor 1e-8; standardized residuals use scale floor 1e-4; queries are batched in 128 rows.
Local moments average squared standardized ILR residuals over K-1 coordinates, Gaussian-smooth them over standardized covariates, and shrink the ratio toward 1 by prior mass.

Moment ratios are clipped to [.25,4]; a common row-scalar multiplies all ILR scales, preserving their within-row ratios. The correction blends are 0,.5,1; bandwidths .5*sqrt(6),sqrt(6); prior masses 10,50.

Nested three-fold training selection uses swapped pseudo-calibration/evaluation halves; the row-weighted alpha-averaged log arithmetic mean ILR-box volume is minimized, with smaller blend breaking ties.

The selector uses exact finite ranks, Gaussian-loss fallback for unavailable ranks or invalid radii/objectives, and a neutral tiny-sample fallback. Realized fallback frequencies and selected settings are not retained.

Global constant scale multiplication cancels its conformal radius, apart from clipping. At alpha .05, 18 internal calibration observations are insufficient for a finite rank; 19 suffice. Numerical invariance assertions are source checks, not a scientific ablation.
Independent final calibration uses ceil((m+1)*(1-alpha)) order statistic with infinity when unavailable, and closed membership. It is not selected on calibration labels.
The unscaled ILR comparator sets scales to one at the same center. Simplex max uses a joint coordinate maximum. Bonferroni calibrates K simplex coordinates at alpha/K, not ILR coordinates.

Mass is uniform-simplex probability content estimated at 128 test contexts using 1024 shared Dirichlet(1) probes; utility equals (1-mass)*max(0,1-absolute_coverage_error/(1-alpha)). Errors are absolute before averaging.
IID covariates are uniform on [-1.5,1.5]^6, logistic-normal noise standard deviation is .25, Dirichlet concentration is 4+35/(1+exp(2*x0)), and gamma coordinates are floored at 1e-12 before closure.
The fixed mean is .7*sin(XW)+.3*x0*cos(j), with W[l,j]=sin(l*(K-1)+j+1)/3. Shift changes only test X to clipped N(.8,1) in [-2.5,3], changing covariate support as well as frequency.
Independent random streams use SeedSequence([seed,case,split,202611]); reference split index is 3. Frozen resources are checked for numeric row-content disjointness, positivity, closure and hashes.

Per-context mass resolution is 1/1024. Zero hits have a one-sided .95 upper bound 1-.05**(1/1024)=.00292124, not zero mass. Averaged plugin context standard errors do not quantify joint mass uncertainty.

The evaluator resamples seed blocks 20000 times using RNG seed 62845. Paired utility intervals have optional tail probability .05/(2*54); volume intervals are unadjusted. Repeated uncertainty summaries are deduplicated.

Constant-input queries use training-mean features; nonidentity permutations rotate calibration and test rows separately. Whole-simplex and zero-radius references are degenerate metric controls, not useful calibrated baselines.
The evaluated environment requires CPython 3.11 or 3.12 and NumPy 1.26.4 with native Linux isolation. No external dataset is downloaded for the synthetic study.

The matched final evidence does not contain a selector-only Gaussian-versus-rank comparison or an original-initializer comparison. The earlier configurations are development evidence, not final ablations.
IID and shifted scaled-ILR absolute coverage errors are 0.013562011718750005 and 0.13034261067708333, respectively.
The scaled-ILR mean utility is 0.661819668104677, mass 0.3034934467739529, and aggregate utility gap to the strongest standard comparator is 0.011594669497844157.

Favorable simplex-baseline contrasts concentrate in IID Dirichlet K8; all shifted utility differences are negative and all shifted mass differences positive. This is not uniform dominance.

Joint unscaled maximum-residual and coordinatewise Bonferroni rectangles are described by Fan and Sesia, Algorithms S2 and S1 respectively; simplex intersection is imposed by this evaluation, not attributed to that source.
